newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens, focus on reserve rate.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens, focus on reserve rate.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in slow trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said the softening was due to wild unfounded rumours of riots in Jakarta, but operators were generally calm.
"It did rattle the market briefly, but the underlying concern remains the reserve rate tomorrow," one said.
Banks have to comply with a new reserve rate of five percent on Wednesday, up from three percent at present. Dealers estimate the new rate would drain five to eight trillion rupiah from the market.

But many dealers said that operators had had plenty of time to prepare as the new rate was announced last year. However, some remained cautious despite a sharp decline in overnight money to one percent from 8.0/9.0 percent.
The central bank, which offered overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) at six percent earlier, removed the offer due to heavy inflows.

Some dealers said liquidity was expected to remain steady on Wednesday because of anticipated central bank supply of some 3.3 trillion rupiah, in addition to possible offers of repo papers and short-term securities (SBPUs) to help the market.
"I think the market should be okay tomorrow. There could be some uptrend in the morning and it may decline later," one said.
Dealers said fears over possible tightening capped the dollar on the upside at the 2,406.5 level despite rumours of riots due to political protests in Jakarta.
Hundreds of supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri staged a protest outside parliament house in a show of strength for the ousted minority party leader ahead of May's general elections.
Chanting slogans and waving banners reading "Mega or Nothing," about 1,500 to 2,000 people demonstrated outside the building in central Jakarta for most of the day.
But there was no violence, police said.
Spot rupiah softened to 2,406.25/06.40 at 1030 GMT from an opening of 2,403.75/04.25. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,405.8/06.1 and 2,405.00/05.75, respectively.
Tom/next swap was at 0.35/0.43 and overnight at par/0.1.
Dealers said swap rates, which declined in the morning, remained stable in the afternoon despite on-going rumours.
One-month swaps were at 12.25/12.45, two at 23.5/24.5, three at 35.75/36.75 and six at 71.00/71.75 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,401/2,593 and the conversion band to 2,401/2,449 on Tuesday.
